explanation: Newton's First Law states that an object will remain at rest or move in a straight line at constant speed unless an external force acts on it.
Binary search works by repeatedly dividing a sorted list into halves and checking whether the target lies in the left or right half.
Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too well, including noise, which reduces its performance on new data.
A stack follows the Last In First Out principle, like a stack of plates where the last plate added is the first removed.
Ohm’s Law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage and inversely proportional to resistance.
Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem until a base case is reached.
An operating system is software that manages hardware resources and provides services to applications and users.
Time complexity describes how the execution time of an algorithm grows as the size of the input increases.
Probability measures how likely an event is to occur, expressed as a number between 0 and 1.
Database indexing improves query performance by allowing faster data retrieval, similar to an index in a book.
Newton’s Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Merge sort divides an array into smaller parts, sorts them, and then merges the sorted parts to produce a sorted array.
The bias-variance tradeoff describes the balance between model simplicity and flexibility to achieve good generalization.
A linked list is a collection of nodes where each node stores data and a reference to the next node.
Coulomb’s Law explains the force of attraction or repulsion between two charged particles.
Dynamic programming solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing results.
Process scheduling decides which process runs on the CPU at a given time to maximize efficiency and fairness.
Space complexity measures how much memory an algorithm needs as the input size increases.
A random variable assigns numerical values to the outcomes of a random experiment.
ACID properties ensure reliable database transactions through atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.
Work is done when a force causes displacement, and power measures how fast the work is done.
Quick sort selects a pivot element, partitions the array around it, and recursively sorts the subarrays.
Cross validation evaluates a model by training and testing it on different subsets of the data to assess generalization.
A hash table stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to quickly locate values.
A Bernoulli trial is a random experiment with only two possible outcomes, usually success or failure.
Paging is a memory management technique that divides memory into fixed-size blocks to avoid fragmentation.
Concurrency allows multiple tasks to make progress during overlapping time periods.
Matrix addition is performed by adding corresponding elements of matrices with the same dimensions.
The client-server model divides tasks between service providers (servers) and service requesters (clients).
Transaction management ensures that database operations are executed reliably and consistently.
Friction is a force that resists the motion between two surfaces that are in contact.
Heap sort builds a heap from the input data and repeatedly removes the maximum element to produce a sorted array.
Gradient descent is an optimization method that minimizes a function by moving in the direction of the steepest decrease.
A circular queue connects the end of the queue back to the beginning to efficiently use memory.
Pascal’s triangle is a triangular array of numbers where each number is the sum of the two above it.
Virtual memory allows programs to use more memory than physically available by using disk space as an extension of RAM.
Deadlock prevention avoids deadlocks by ensuring that at least one of the necessary deadlock conditions cannot occur.
The dot product of two vectors is found by multiplying corresponding components and summing the results.
REST is an architectural style for designing networked applications using stateless communication and standard HTTP methods.
Two-phase locking ensures serializability in databases by dividing locking into growing and shrinking phases.
Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity, describing how difficult it is to stop the object.
Counting sort counts the number of occurrences of each element and uses this information to place elements in order.
Support Vector Machines classify data by finding a decision boundary that maximizes the margin between classes.
A deque is a double-ended queue that allows insertion and deletion from both the front and rear.
The binomial distribution models the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials.
Thread synchronization coordinates the execution of threads to prevent conflicts when accessing shared resources.
Eigenvalues represent scaling factors associated with linear transformations of vectors.
IP addressing assigns unique numerical identifiers to devices so they can communicate over a network.
Normalization reduces redundancy by structuring data efficiently, while denormalization improves read performance by duplicating data.
Bayes theorem describes how to update probabilities when new evidence is available.
Angular velocity describes how fast an object rotates around an axis, measured in radians per second.
Shell sort improves insertion sort by comparing elements that are far apart and gradually reducing the gap.
Decision trees classify data by making a sequence of decisions based on feature values.
A sparse matrix contains mostly zero values, allowing efficient storage by recording only non-zero elements.
A geometric progression is a sequence where each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by a constant ratio.
Page replacement algorithms decide which memory pages to remove when new pages need to be loaded into memory.
A race condition occurs when multiple threads access shared data and the final result depends on execution order.
Matrix multiplication combines rows and columns of two matrices to produce a new matrix.
Client-server architecture separates responsibilities between service providers and service requesters.
Checkpointing saves the state of a system so it can recover from failures without restarting completely.
Moment of inertia measures how resistant an object is to rotational motion, depending on mass distribution.
Comb sort improves bubble sort by comparing elements at a shrinking gap until the list is sorted.
Logistic regression predicts probabilities for binary outcomes using a sigmoid function.
A bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic structure used to test set membership with possible false positives.
Permutations count the number of ways items can be arranged when order matters.
Deadlock detection identifies cycles in resource allocation to determine whether a deadlock exists.
A mutex lock ensures that only one thread can access a shared resource at a time.
Eigenvectors indicate directions that remain unchanged in direction under a linear transformation.
An API gateway acts as a single entry point that routes requests to appropriate backend services.
Write-ahead logging records changes before they are applied, ensuring database recovery after crashes.
Angular acceleration describes how quickly angular velocity changes over time.
Tim sort combines insertion sort and merge sort to efficiently sort real-world data.
Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classifier based on Bayes theorem with an assumption of feature independence.
Disjoint set union manages a collection of non-overlapping sets using union and find operations.
Combinations count the number of ways to choose items from a set when order does not matter.
Memory fragmentation occurs when free memory is divided into small non-contiguous blocks, reducing efficiency.
A spinlock is a lock where a thread repeatedly checks for availability instead of sleeping.
SVD decomposes a matrix into singular vectors and values, useful for dimensionality reduction.
A reverse proxy forwards client requests to backend servers and improves security and performance.
Shadow paging maintains consistency by keeping separate old and new versions of modified database pages.
Torque causes an object to rotate and depends on the applied force and its distance from the axis of rotation.
Intro sort begins with quick sort and switches to heap sort when recursion depth becomes too large.
KNN classifies data points based on the majority class among their nearest neighbors.
A suffix array stores all suffixes of a string in sorted order to support efficient pattern matching.
Conditional probability measures the likelihood of an event occurring given that another event has already occurred.
Memory paging divides processes into fixed-size pages to allow efficient memory allocation.
Atomic operations are executed completely without interruption, ensuring data consistency in concurrent systems.
Covariance indicates how two variables change together, showing whether they increase or decrease simultaneously.
A CDN distributes content across multiple servers to deliver data faster to users.
Write skew is an anomaly where concurrent transactions read overlapping data and write disjoint updates, leading to inconsistency.
Centrifugal force is an apparent force observed in a rotating frame that seems to push objects outward from the center.
Bitonic sort works by forming bitonic sequences and recursively merging them to produce a sorted sequence.
Linear regression models the relationship between variables by fitting a straight line that minimizes prediction error.
Persistent data structures preserve previous versions of themselves when modified, allowing access to older states.
Random sampling selects a subset of data such that every element has an equal chance of being chosen.
Memory compaction rearranges processes in memory to reduce fragmentation and improve utilization.
Lock-free algorithms allow multiple threads to operate on shared data without using locks, ensuring system progress.
Correlation measures the strength and direction of the relationship between two variables.
Service-oriented architecture structures applications as a collection of loosely coupled services.
Checkpoint recovery restores a system to a previously saved state after a failure occurs.
